correctness.rationale: Using the standard generator columns \(g_x=(1,x)^T\), a minimal nontrivial recovery set for a target has odd cardinality and therefore at least three. A recovery triple, after translating by the target, is exactly the three nonzero vectors of a two-dimensional subspace. For odd \(m\), the exact partial two-spread theorem of Năstase--Sissokho at \(q=2,t=2,r=1\) gives \((2^m-5)/3\) disjoint planes. The upper bound does not assume locality three: if one more nontrivial disjoint recovery set existed, counting forces every such set to be a triple and leaves exactly one nonzero vector uncovered; XOR of every plane triple and of all nonzero vectors is zero, forcing the leftover vector to be zero, a contradiction. A fresh independent exact replay verified the explicit maximum partial-spread witnesses and every target at \(m=3,5\).
correctness.risk: The infinite existence step depends on the cited exact partial-spread theorem; the finite replay is corroborative only.

value.rationale: Odd dimension is precisely the case where a full two-spread is impossible and the classical Reed--Muller availability story is subtler. The theorem closes a natural open all-symbol family with an exact infinite formula and shows why allowing larger recovery sets cannot beat the finite-geometric construction.
value.risk: The result determines multiplicity, not all-symbol batch multiplicity or classification of every extremal recovery family.

final_claim: For every odd integer \(m\ge3\), the binary first-order Reed-Muller code \(\mathrm{RM}_2(1,m)\) has exact all-symbol PIR multiplicity \((2^m-2)/3\): after reserving the target singleton, exactly \((2^m-5)/3\) pairwise disjoint nontrivial recovery sets are possible.
limitations: Binary first-order Reed--Muller codes with odd \(m\ge3\) only.
No all-symbol batch claim and no classification of all extremal recovery families.
